purpose: Separate reproducible execution architecture from public strategy claims and preserve the sealed intraday pullback/reclaim route unless deterministic evidence supersedes it.

source_policy.tier_1: official exchange/framework documentation or primary research with explicit methods
source_policy.tier_2: open-source strategy/code with inspectable rules but no accepted independent economics
source_policy.tier_3: community/video/discussion claims used only for hypothesis and failure-mode discovery

accepted_sources.finding: BingX exposes public market data and order-book depth, but the current ZEL historical corpus has not proven event-time L2, aggressor trades, queue position, own-order latency or partial-fill history.
accepted_sources.transfer: Keep true microstructure and maker-spread-capture backtests blocked until immutable historical data and account execution receipts exist.

accepted_sources.finding: L2/L3 data drives depth-aware matching and partial fills; higher-granularity books cannot be reconstructed from bars or lower-level data.
accepted_sources.transfer: Bar-only candidate must use conservative next-bar/taker execution and cannot claim queue, maker-fill or microprice economics.

accepted_sources.finding: Market orders walk L2/L3 depth and may partially fill; L1/bar simulation cannot reproduce the same depth behavior.
accepted_sources.transfer: Require 2x-cost, wider-slippage and plus-one-bar stress before economic acceptance.

accepted_sources.finding: Production architecture separates market-data-driven Controllers from order-lifecycle Executors and supports directional, market-making, arbitrage and grid families.
accepted_sources.transfer: Keep signal generation isolated from execution ownership; do not combine strategy families before standalone positive economics.

accepted_sources.finding: MarketDataProvider, Controllers and Executors are separate components, enabling testable signal and order lifecycle boundaries.
accepted_sources.transfer: Future ZEL runtime integration must preserve candidate/decision/execution separation; research code remains isolated now.

accepted_sources.finding: Uses trend bias, pullback/reclaim, momentum confirmation and ATR exits on 1-5 minute charts.
accepted_sources.transfer: Supports the archetype only; its markets, parameters and reported popularity cannot authorize ZEL thresholds or economics.

accepted_sources.finding: Uses higher-timeframe bias, lower-timeframe pullback/reclaim, optional volume/session filters and cooldown.
accepted_sources.transfer: Confirms common design decomposition; optional filters remain prohibited until base edge is positive and tested independently.

accepted_sources.finding: BTC 5-minute pullback continuation using ordered EMAs and reclaim logic.
accepted_sources.transfer: Timeframe/family is relevant, but EMA thresholds are not imported because no independent cost-after validation is supplied.

accepted_sources.finding: Cryptocurrency returns, volume and volatility exhibit intraday temporal structure relevant to algorithmic participation.
accepted_sources.transfer: Session/time concentration must be reported and stressed; event/session filters cannot be selected from sealed OOS labels.

accepted_sources.finding: Adaptive market making depends on changing market conditions, granular data and sub-strategy selection.
accepted_sources.transfer: Do not adopt market making without historical book/execution evidence; router selection is deferred until standalone families pass.

search_coverage.community_video_disposition: No community or video claim was accepted as deterministic economic evidence in this run; reproducible code, exact costs and independent OOS receipts were absent or not verifiable from search results.

cross_source_findings: Profitable architecture cannot be inferred from indicator popularity or headline win rate.
Directional pullback/reclaim is repeatedly implemented as higher-timeframe bias plus lower-timeframe confirmation, but thresholds are market-specific and require independent cost-after replay.
Market making and order-flow strategies require event-time book/trade and execution evidence that the current historical corpus does not provide.
Signal logic and execution lifecycle should remain separate so costs, fills, stops and timeouts can be independently verified.
Generation-1 should remain one family with bounded dimensions; adding volume, session, VWAP, trailing, partial or router logic before base positivity would create attribution and overfit risk.

architecture_effect.reason: The expanded evidence supports the decomposition and execution conservatism but does not provide deterministic evidence strong enough to replace or broaden the sealed design.
